description: Composite figure of four EBSD-derived grain-boundary panels for a low-density Fe-28Mn-8Al-1C steel. (a) is a grain-boundary map of the undeformed steel dominated by solid black boundary traces (HAGBs) outlining equiaxed grains, with only sparse red LAGB segments; a 50 µm scale bar is at lower-left. (b) is the CR 30% map, a dense network in which red LAGB segments form a large fraction of the traced boundaries mixed with black HAGB lines; scale bar 20 µm. (c) is the CR 90% map, overwhelmingly red before/overlaid by black lines, arranged as elongated, banded/rolling-direction features that are much finer; scale bar 5 µm. (d) is a bar-frequency histogram, x-axis "Misorientation/deg" from 0 to 60 in 10° ticks, y-axis "Frequency/%" from 0 to 70 in 10% ticks, with legend entries "Underformed" (orange), "CR 30%" (green) and "CR 90%" (purple). All three distributions peak sharply at low misorientation (~2-3°) and the undeformed curve has a second dominant peak at 60° reaching ~60% frequency, whereas the CR 30% and CR 90% curves are depleted at 60°. The group shows the deformation-driven LAGB/HAGB transition. Note the caption calls (d) a "comparison map", but it is rendered as a histogram.

subfigures.description: Grain-boundary map of the undeformed steel; predominantly solid black HAGB traces enclosing equiaxed grains, with only rare red LAGB segments. Scale bar 50 µm.
Grain-boundary map after CR 30%; a dense mixed network with a large proportion of red LAGB segments interspersed with black HAGB lines. Scale bar 20 µm.
Grain-boundary map after CR 90%; boundaries are dominated by red LAGB segments arranged as fine elongated, banded features. Scale bar 5 µm.

Bar histogram of boundary misorientation: x-axis 'Misorientation/deg' (0-60), y-axis 'Frequency/%' (0-70); legend 'Underformed' (orange), 'CR 30%' (green), 'CR 90%' (purple). Low-angle peak for all; a strong 60° peak only for the undeformed condition.

observations.observation: The undeformed grain-boundary map (a) is dominated by solid black HAGB lines outlining equiaxed grains, with only sparse red LAGB segments.
The CR 90% map (c) is overwhelmingly composed of red LAGB segments arranged as elongated banded features, whereas the CR 30% map (b) contains a large but lesser red fraction mixed with black HAGBs.
Scale bars are printed as 50 µm in (a), 20 µm in (b) and 5 µm in (c), indicating progressively finer observation length scale with increasing deformation.
In panel (d) the undeformed distribution shows a strong peak at a misorientation of 60° reaching about 60% frequency, while the CR 30% and CR 90% curves are almost depleted at 60°.
All three curves in (d) show their highest low-angle population near 2-3° misorientation, consistent with the LAGB-dominated networks in (b) and (c).
The caption states the solid black lines represent HAGBs while the red lines denote LAGBs.
The caption labels panel (d) a 'comparison map of grain boundaries', although the rendered panel is a misorientation-frequency histogram.
The undeformed steel exhibits predominantly 94.65% high-angle grain boundaries (HAGBs).
After 30% CR reduction the proportion of low-angle grain boundaries (LAGBs) increases to 89.4% (Figure 6d).
With deformation to CR 90%, LAGBs account for 94.1% (Figure 6d).
Sharp peaks at a misorientation angle of 60° correspond to twin boundaries 60<111> in the undeformed condition.
